title: quickbench-runtime-slab-dollar-timeline-draft
body:
Purpose:
A compact, reproducible quickbench to surface trade-offs between runtime slab allocation strategies and dollars-per-response over a 24h synthetic surge. This is intentionally a lightweight write-up for product + infra to decide follow-ups, not the canonical lab report.

Scope and goal:
- Compare three slab strategies: fixed-slab (1x), slab-with-burst (1x+burst), auto-slab (elastic slots).
- Measure user-facing response-time (ms) at p50/p90/p99 and cost-per-1k-requests ($) across steady load vs 10x microbursts.
- Keep model constant: llama-3-13b-quant (perference for compact-medium families).
- Capture impact of small-session vs long-session mixes.

Env / test harness:
- Region: us-west2, single-zone for deterministic NVLink behavior.
- GPUs: 4x A100-80GB per cluster.
- Runtime: rwd-runtime v2.3.1 with KV-cache prefetch enabled.
- Batch window: 10ms programmable.
- Synthetic traffic: Poisson baseline at 250 qps; 6 microbursts of 2500 qps for 30s every 3h (24h horizon).
- Cost model: infra cost metric normalized to $ per 1000 requests, including BURST premium (extra nodes billed), and amortized KV cache overhead.

Key numbers (24h aggregate, model fixed):
Table format (rows): strategy | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | 1k-req $ | burst-penalty $
fixed-slab | 42 | 110 | 340 | 0.82 | +0.00
slab-with-burst | 48 | 95 | 280 | 1.05 | +0.16
auto-slab | 55 | 125 | 260 | 0.93 | +0.09

ASCII mini-chart: p99 vs $/1k (lower is better on both)
p99(ms)  | 260      280      340
$/1k     | 0.82    0.93    1.05
labels   | fixed   auto    burst

Observations / short analysis:
- Fixed-slab gives best steady-dollar (0.82) and surprisingly strong p50, but p99 spikes to 340ms during microbursts — worst tail behavior. Good for cost-conscious background workloads where occasional tail is acceptable.
- Slab-with-burst reduces p99 compared to fixed (280ms) thanks to temporary extra capacity, but shows the highest $/1k (1.05) because burst nodes are billed and underutilized outside spikes. Useful for customer-facing real-time apps that must avoid long tails and can pay a premium.
- Auto-slab (elastic slots) sits in the middle: better p99 than fixed under bursts (260ms) and lower cost than explicit burst policy, but p90 and p50 drift slightly up — suggests oscillation/scale-up latency.
- Burst-penalty column shows bookkeeping: slab-with-burst has explicit premium; auto-slab amortizes some of that but still pays for scale churning.

Micro-observations from traces:
- Scale-up latency (node attach + warmup) is the dominant cause of p99 tail in auto-slab; warm-started cache hit-rate correlates strongly with lower tail.
- Fixed-slab shows slot contention: increased queuing at the decode worker rather than model forward time.
- Slab-with-burst had a handful of cold-restarts during a single long surge which inflated cost without improving tail consistently — tuning needed.

Quick recommendations / experiment matrix (next steps):
1) For 2-week pilot: run slab-with-burst but reduce burst node TTL to 60s and prewarm KV cache policy. Hypothesis: reduces cost by ~10–15% while retaining p99 improvements.
2) For auto-slab: experiment with predictive pre-attach (attach nodes ~12–18s before forecasted microbursts) using simple exponential smoothing of request-rate. Measure p99 and cost delta.
3) Hybrid approach: baseline fixed-slab sized for 90th-percentile sustained; small auto-slab budget for microbursts to limit p99 without large dollars.

Appendix: brief checklist for full lab report:
- Repeat across 3 model families (13b, 33b, 70b-compact)
- Add network-proximity variants (edge vs core)
- Break out decode vs model time vs queue time in seconds for every percentile
- Validate with real traffic traces (prod anonymized)
- Include energy consumption if infra tags require sustainability numbers

Notes and questions:
- This quickbench omits GPU utilization granularity; we should record util% and MIG partition impact next run.
- Any objections to using 13b for follow-ups? It reduces total lab cost and exposes scaling behavior but may not capture 70b-specific memory-induced tail effects.

Contact: Priya Nair (pri@redwood.ai).
